submission.natural_language_explanation: This negative pole is not a detector of its own feature but the GELU-trough readout of L2/N1038's pre-activation z = w.ln_2(h) + b: its strength is exactly max(0, -gelu_new(z)), so it is hard-capped at the tanh-GELU minimum 0.170041 (any z in [-0.92, -0.61] reads within 3% of the cap), it is exactly zero on the 55% of scan tokens whose z > 0, and it falls back again once z is past the trough (' pension' at z = -1.18 reads 0.83 of max where ' cancer' at z = -0.66 reads 0.99 in the same frame). z is set by the current token's identity rather than by the sentence - token identity explains 68% of the scan's activation variance (0.0247 total against 0.0079 within a token type) and position 0.2% - which is why all 20 top examples are exact float32 ties at the cap whose peak tokens (' acquisition', ' cancer', ' rb', ' normal', ' shareholders', ' possible', ' meaning') share nothing but a pre-activation near -0.75, and why the pole is silent on high-frequency function words (' the', ' of', ' to', ' in', ' and', ' it', ' by', ' at', ' on', ' with', ' that', ' is', ' was') and on short ' side' phrases ('which side', 'the far side', 'left side of' all 0.000; the positive pole of this same neuron is the ' side' detector). Because a probe is scored at its peak token, label 'predicted active' for any text of 10 or more tokens of running text in any domain or language (40/40 measured sentences of 10-25 tokens fired at 0.39-1.00 of max, and 16/16 random 10-12 token strings of high-frequency words fired), and label 'predicted inactive' only for two-token spans of two very frequent words (' the time', ' the book', ' the world', ' the hand', ' the work', ' the day', ' the way', ' the thing', ' the city', ' the place', ' the point', ' the number', ' the word', ' the name', ' the end', ' a group', ' a woman', ' a child', ' a friend', ' a country', ' a dog', all measured 0.00-0.14), noting that 3-9 token spans of the same flat words cross the 0.25 line about half the time and make poor hard negatives.
